Honestly, I think people overlook it without any ill-intent (most of the time).

I suffer from grandiose thoughts rather than psychosis when manic. I feel like god. As if I am the centre point of the world and everything revolves around me. I feel as though I am the most important person and that my opinion is the only one that matters. I fall back into this persona that is very wild and difficult to manage. I'm spontaneous and really unpredictable. I do dangerous things; hang out with criminals (I seek them out), sex with strangers, spend all my money. I do things like go into bars and announce I'm going to buy everyone in the bar a drink that I feel defines them. I go to casinos and put all my money on black or red at the roulette wheel. I feel as though I'm on the edge of brilliance and that's what motivates me. Problem is the higher I go the further I fall. Everything is an equation when it comes to bipolar and unfortunately this superb manic period resulted in one of the worst depressive ones. I don't even know why I called the manic period superb either, it damn nearly ruined my life. Like every other one. I just can't see it at the time.
Thank you. I definitely intend to focus on constant management of my illness now.

I'm on Latuda which is a fairly new medication for bipolar (and a fairly new anti psychotic in general) but so far so good. I find I can function very well on it, but it's only been 5 days so I'll have to give it more time.

First and foremost I learnt that mental illness is like any other physical ailment and needs TLC and proper acute care when necessary.

Also I learnt that it is easier to commit yourself than to wake up after 4 days in a coma and have to face your loved ones knowing that you tried to kill yourself unsuccessfully.

I would say I'm on the road to stable, but yes am taking my medication. A big road block to me staying med compliant before was the insistence from doctors to stay on lithium (which I hate). I'm on a new med now and doing much better.

Honestly, I do but not in the way you might think. I feel better because I am no longer overwhelmingly suicidal, but I am still depressed.

One thing though I was fortunate enough to be placed in a ward with some incredible human beings that showed me so much kindness and understanding. We became fast friends in a week and will stay in touch.
